earnings.title: HYATT REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS
highlights: Diluted EPS was $0.60 and Adjusted Diluted EPS was $1.27
Net income attributable to Hyatt Hotels Corporation was $58 million and Adjusted Net Income was $122 million
Comparable system-wide hotels RevPAR increased 7.2%, compared to the third quarter of 2025
Comparable system-wide all-inclusive resorts Net Package RevPAR decreased 2.5%, compared to the third quarter of 2025
Repurchased 867,109 shares of Class A common stock during the third quarter for an aggregate purchase price of $147 million.

quotes.text: Our strong third quarter results, including 15% growth in Gross Fees, reinforce the strength of Hyatt's differentiated brands, growing commercial platform, and asset-light business model.

items.heading: We are subject to macroeconomic and other factors beyond our control, as well as the business, financial, operating, and other risks of the hospitality industry, all of which may adversely affect our financial results and growth.
items.group: Risks Related to the Hospitality Industry

items.heading: The hospitality industry is cyclical and adverse global economic conditions or low levels of economic growth could adversely affect our revenues and profitability as well as cause a decline in or limitation of our future growth.
items.group: Risks Related to the Hospitality Industry

items.heading: Because we operate in a highly competitive industry, our revenues, profits, or market share could be harmed if we are unable to compete effectively, and new distribution channels, including potential AI platforms, alternatives to traditional hotels, and industry consolidation among our competitors may negatively impact our business.

Significant increases in the volume of sales made through third-party internet travel intermediaries could have an adverse impact on consumer loyalty to our brand and could negatively affect our revenues and profits.

If we are unable to establish and maintain key distribution arrangements for our properties or hospitality-related businesses, the demand for our rooms, hospitality-related services, and revenues could decrease.
The risks of doing business internationally, or in a particular country or region, could lower our revenues, increase our costs, reduce our profits, or disrupt our business.
